name: Invoices a payment could settle
brief:
A payment of `target` pounds arrived without a reference. The open invoices are `amounts`, and several invoices may share an amount. Accounts wants every way the payment could settle at most `k` whole invoices exactly.

Write `invoice_matches(amounts, target, k)`, which returns each distinct way as an ascending list of amounts, with the lists in Python's order for lists. Two ways that differ only in which of two equal invoices they use are the same way.

Example. For `[20, 50, 30, 20, 10]`, a target of 50 and `k = 2`, the ways are `[20, 30]` and `[50]`. The way `[10, 20, 20]` uses three invoices, one more than `k` allows.
constraints: $1 \le n \le 20$ invoices of £1 to £1,000, $1 \le$ `target` $\le 20{,}000$ and $1 \le k \le 20$.
A search that skips repeated amounts and stops at `k` invoices is fast enough.
All the tests in a run share one 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Sort the amounts and walk them in order. At each depth skip an amount equal to the one just tried there, and stop a branch when it holds `k` invoices or the next amount is more than what is left.

examples.note: `[10, 20, 20]` also makes £50 but needs three invoices.
The two £5 invoices are alike, so `[5, 15]` is listed once.

how: Submit runs 12 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value. Unlike listing the combinations that make a total, at most `k` invoices may be used, so the walk is capped in depth as well as in sum.
notes: After sorting, equal amounts sit side by side, and trying a repeat at the same depth would rebuild a way already listed.
A branch stops when it holds `k` invoices, or when the next amount is more than what is left, since every later amount is larger.
The walk visits each distinct way at most once per prefix, so its cost is bounded by $O(n \cdot 2^n)$ and is far less with the caps.

planted.slip: Without skipping a repeated amount at the same depth, the same way is listed once for each choice of equal invoices.
Leaving out the check on `k` lists ways with too many invoices.
Staying on the same amount after taking it lets one invoice be settled twice.
